items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: One, Bugaloosers, Gary, out in the country, La Plague, anywhere.

ctx.x: About four funerals. Well, that's about once a week, in other words. You'd be out in the street. So there was a lot of work for jump-up bands.

Oh, yeah. Well, you see, we did write some out here in New Orleans, but the average time, these bands was going away from town. One, Bugaloosers, Gary, out in the country, La Plague, anywhere. All of them was going on weekends like that. And Monday nights, well, economy, co-op, Riddling, Aging Park, Napoleon Avenue Hall, everybody would be playing Monday night in a different hall, see. And them that wasn't going out of town, they'd be on the streets all day Sunday, you know, advertising for dances in town, you…
Well, what kind of organization would hire a jump-up band for a funeral rather than an organized band?
